issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may run rough, refuse to start, or shut off while you are driving. Many warning lights can come on at once.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank can stop working. Honda and Acura recalled a large group of cars, including these NSX years, to replace the pump module.
issues.next: Check your VIN on Acura's recall site or nhtsa.gov/recalls. The new pump module is free at an Acura dealer. If the car stalls, get safely off the road and have it towed rather than restarting it again and again.

issues.t: Fuel can leak from the tank crossover pipe (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline around the car, or wet spots or drips of fuel under the middle of the car.
issues.why: The NSX has left and right fuel tanks joined by a crossover pipe. The couplers on that pipe can leak, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive or park it in a garage. Check the VIN for the recall; dealers replace both fuel tanks free.

issues.t: Center brake light can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The high center brake light, or all the brake lights, don't come on when you press the brake. A blown-fuse or bulb warning may show.
issues.why: Road vibration can loosen the screws on the center brake light's circuit board. It can short and blow the brake light fuse, so cars behind you get no warning.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights while you press the pedal. Check the VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the center brake light free.

issues.t: Dead 12V battery from audio unit staying on
issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting for a day or more because the 12V battery has run flat. The screen may have shown "USB Not Responding".
issues.why: Acura found the audio unit may not shut down fully after the car is turned off, so it slowly drains the 12V battery.
issues.next: Jump or charge the battery, then ask an Acura dealer about bulletin B19040B and the audio software update. A battery maintainer helps if the car sits often.

issues.t: Won't start on first press of the start button
issues.sym: You press the start button and the car doesn't come on, then it works on a later try. A stored code B12C5 may show up at the dealer.
issues.why: Acura issued a bulletin for certain 2017 cars that may not start on the first press, and extended the warranty on some 2017 cars.
issues.next: Note how often it happens and ask an Acura dealer to check for bulletin B20-050 and any warranty extension on your VIN.

issues.t: Power system won't start from a blown fuse
issues.sym: The car won't go into ready mode and the power system won't start, even though the 12V battery seems fine.
issues.why: A blown fuse (fuse B5) can stop the hybrid power system from starting. Acura issued a service bulletin on finding and fixing the cause.
issues.next: Don't keep swapping fuses yourself; a fuse that blew may blow again. Have an Acura dealer diagnose it using bulletin BTS171001.

issues.t: Rough or failed shifting from debris in the dual-clutch transmission
issues.sym: Harsh, delayed or missed shifts and a warning light. Code P26C3 may be stored.
issues.why: Acura issued a bulletin about possible debris inside the 9-speed dual-clutch transmission on early cars affecting the shift system.
issues.next: Have an Acura dealer read the codes. If the transmission can't go into neutral, the car must be moved on dollies or a flatbed, not dragged.

issues.t: Check engine light from thermostat seal (P0128)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0128. The engine may take a long time to warm up and the heater may feel weak at first.
issues.why: The inner seal of the thermostat can come loose, so coolant keeps flowing and the engine runs cooler than the computer expects.
issues.next: Not urgent, but get it fixed. Ask an Acura dealer about bulletin B17-048, which covers replacing the thermostat.

issues.t: Check engine light from fuel filler EVAP leak
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0455 or P0456 (evaporative system leak). You may also notice a faint fuel smell near the filler.
issues.why: A small leak around the fuel filler neck lets fuel vapor escape. Acura's bulletin says to replace a specific part rather than the whole fill pipe.
issues.next: First make sure the fuel cap or filler door seal is tight. If the light stays on, a dealer can use bulletin BTS170202.

issues.t: Outside door handle doesn't retract
issues.sym: The flush door handle stays sticking out or won't pull back in after the car is locked or driven.
issues.why: Acura sent many dealer messages about outer door handles on 2017-2019 cars not retracting properly.
issues.next: Have the dealer look at it while the car may still be under warranty. A handle stuck out can be damaged and may not lock properly.

issues.t: Door window stops moving (regulator)
issues.sym: A door window won't go up or down, moves slowly, or makes grinding noises. The glass may get stuck partly open.
issues.why: Acura sent repeated dealer messages about the window regulator failing on 2018-2019 cars.
issues.next: Avoid forcing the glass. Have the regulator replaced; a window stuck open leaves the car exposed to rain and theft.

issues.t: Rattle from the door tweeter area
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter near the small door speaker at the top of the door, often over bumps or with music playing.
issues.why: Acura issued many dealer messages and bulletin B19-010 about rattles near the door tweeters on 2017-2021 cars.
issues.next: Have the dealer find the loose part; the fix is usually padding or securing trim.

issues.t: Wind noise from door glass
issues.sym: A whooshing or whistling noise at highway speed from the side windows.
issues.why: The door glass may not seal fully against the weatherstrip. Acura issued bulletins B19-025 and many dealer messages about side-window wind noise.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check glass alignment and seals.

issues.t: Rattle or noise from the steering wheel
issues.sym: A rattle or buzz from the center of the steering wheel, around the driver's airbag, often on rough roads.
issues.why: Acura looked into steering wheel rattles on 2017-2019 cars and issued more dealer messages about steering wheel noise on 2020-2021 cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect it. Don't try to take the airbag cover apart yourself.

issues.t: Rattle or squeak from the carbon fiber gauge visor
issues.sym: A squeak or rattle from the cover above the gauges, mostly on bumpy roads.
issues.why: Acura investigated many reports of the carbon fiber meter visor rattling on 2017-2018 cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer secure or insulate the visor.

issues.t: Climate control buttons stick or rattle
issues.sym: Buttons on the climate panel stick when pressed or rattle while driving.
issues.why: Acura issued bulletin B19-013 for climate control buttons that stick or rattle.
issues.next: Mention bulletin B19-013 to a dealer.

issues.t: Dashboard creaks
issues.sym: Creaking or ticking from the dashboard, especially over bumps or as the cabin warms up.
issues.why: Parts of the dash rub together. Acura's bulletin B18-064 adds felt padding at the contact points.
issues.next: A dealer can apply the felt fix from bulletin B18-064.

issues.t: Airbag light from internal SRS unit fault
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light stays on. Code U3000-49 is stored.
issues.why: Acura issued bulletin B21100A for an internal failure of the airbag control unit.
issues.next: While the airbag light is on, the airbags may not work in a crash. Get it checked by an Acura dealer soon.

issues.t: Clicking from a wheel area while driving
issues.sym: A clicking or ticking noise from one of the wheels while driving.
issues.why: Acura issued bulletin B21-025 on clicking noises from the wheel area.
issues.next: Have it checked soon to rule out loose wheel or brake parts, then ask the dealer about bulletin B21-025.

issues.t: Electric power steering (EPS) failure
issues.sym: The EPS warning light comes on and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy. It may come back after a restart and then fail again.
issues.why: The NSX uses an electric power steering system. Owners most often trace failures to the aging EPS control unit; water getting past a torn rack boot can also rust the steering motor.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. A shop that knows the NSX can read the blink codes from the service connector; OBD scanners don't see EPS codes.

issues.t: Timing belt and water pump overdue
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A worn belt can snap and stop the engine instantly; a failing water pump may leak coolant or whine.
issues.why: The NSX V6 uses a rubber timing belt that wears out with age and miles. If it breaks, the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.next: Check the records. If there is no proof of a belt and water pump service in roughly the last 90,000 miles or 7 years, have it done before driving hard or far.

issues.t: ABS unit leaking brake fluid
issues.sym: Brake fluid level dropping, wet spots near the ABS unit, an ABS warning light, or a whirring or washing-machine-like noise from the pump.
issues.why: Parts of the anti-lock brake unit, including its pressure accumulator and pump, can leak or wear out on older NSXs.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Low brake fluid is a safety problem. Check the fluid level and have the brakes inspected before driving.

issues.t: Climate control unit fails (leaking capacitors)
issues.sym: The climate display goes blank or acts strangely, the fan is stuck on one speed, or the A/C turns on and off by itself.
issues.why: Small capacitors on the climate control circuit board leak with age, and the leaking fluid corrodes the board.
issues.next: Ask a specialist whether the board can be removed and repaired instead of replaced. Fix it early, before the corrosion spreads.

issues.t: Gauge cluster faults from leaking capacitors
issues.sym: The speedometer reads too low, the brake warning light stays on even though the brakes are fine, or warning lights stay lit after startup.
issues.why: Aging capacitors on the instrument cluster board leak. The fluid can short circuits, and owners warn it can even cause a fire if ignored.
issues.next: Check your speed against a phone GPS. Have the cluster capacitors replaced by someone experienced with NSX clusters.

issues.t: Slow or failing power windows
issues.sym: Windows move slowly, chatter, or go crooked; eventually a window may stop moving.
issues.why: Teeth on the window regulator wear and break, and the motors slow down with age. This is one of the most common NSX complaints.
issues.next: Test both windows. Have the switch, regulator and motor checked before buying a new motor, since slow glass doesn't always mean a bad motor.

issues.t: Clutch wears out (manual cars)
issues.sym: The engine revs rise but the car doesn't speed up to match, especially when accelerating hard or going uphill.
issues.why: The NSX clutch is small for the engine's power. How long it lasts depends heavily on how the car is driven.
issues.next: If you notice slipping, plan a clutch replacement soon; driving on a slipping clutch can damage the flywheel.

issues.t: Check engine light from EVAP system fault
issues.sym: Check engine light on, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A failed part in the evaporative emissions system, such as a valve or hose, lets the computer detect a vapor leak.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap is tight. If the light stays on, have the codes read.

issues.t: Cracked coolant reservoir or brittle hoses
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue around hoses, a sweet smell, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The coolant reservoir can crack and the many long hoses in this mid-engine car get brittle with age.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and replace old hoses together.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers, cam plugs or VTEC solenoid
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil on the engine, or a burning oil smell after driving.
issues.why: Gaskets at the valve covers, rear camshaft plugs and VTEC solenoid harden with age and start to seep.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. Have the leak source found; oil dripping onto hot exhaust parts is a fire risk.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts
issues.sym: Clunks or knocks when shifting or getting on and off the throttle, or extra vibration in the cabin.
issues.why: Rubber engine mounts tear and sag with age.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected; worn ones put extra stress on hoses and exhaust parts.

issues.t: Bose speakers or amplifiers fail
issues.sym: Crackling, distorted or dead speakers, or the radio cutting out.
issues.why: The factory Bose system has amplifiers built into the speakers, and these fail with age.
issues.next: Replace the failed speakers, or replace the system with aftermarket parts.

issues.t: Worn weatherstripping causes wind noise or leaks
issues.sym: Wind noise at speed, or water getting in at the doors, windshield or removable roof panel.
issues.why: Rubber seals around the doors, windshield and roof shrink and tear over time.
issues.next: Inspect the seals and replace any that are cracked or flattened.

issues.t: Immobilizer or key cylinder problems
issues.sym: The car won't start with the key, or the alarm won't arm or disarm from the driver's door.
issues.why: Owners report failures of the immobilizer, ignition switch and the driver's-side key switch for the factory alarm.
issues.next: Try the passenger door lock to arm or disarm the alarm. Have a shop test the immobilizer and ignition switch.
